QF.id: IV Introduction to Interest Rate Derivatives_18

answer.text: Buying a cap and buying a floor simultaneously
Buying a cap and selling a floor simultaneously
Selling both a cap and a floor
Buying two caps with different strikes

explanation.text: The Logic: An interest rate collar is the simultaneous purchase of an interest rate cap and sale of an interest rate floor on the same underlying interest rate, maturity, and notional principal. The Trap: A reverse collar is the opposite structure — simultaneous purchase of an interest rate floor and sale of an interest rate cap on the same underlying, maturity, and notional. Options C and D do not match the collar definition. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-IV workbook (Dec 2025), pages 93 and 154. Collars are listed among OTC interest rate option products.
